_comment: 🧩️ This subset's contribution to the repository test platform — the BMP v3 ✳️any mutation catalog and its dedicated mutate oracle. Discovered by convention (`testContributionDirName` in 🔣️taxonomy.json); the shared stdio manifest (`✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🧪️oracle/🔣️component.json`) already registers `image-bmp` under capability `bmp-raster` for plain create/round-trip coverage — mutation coverage needs its own capability so the two are never conflated, per the wave-7 fleet brief.

oracles.rationale: The same reference BMP encoder/decoder already registered as `image-bmp` (shared stdio manifest), given its own capability for the 7 typed BmpMutation kinds this subset declares. The independent decoder reads both this subset's own encode_bmp output and the oracle's own re-encode, so a mutation's effect is judged the same way regardless of which side produced the bytes. The oracle drives the crate's INDEXED layer, not just its resolved raster: `BmpDecoder::set_indexed_color` for the per-pixel index buffer, `get_palette` for the colour table and `BmpEncoder::encode_with_palette` to write both back as a real indexed BITMAPINFOHEADER. Without that, three of the seven kinds — the palette triple — have nothing to operate on at all, because `load_from_memory` resolves the indices away. Three BITMAPINFOHEADER facts stay outside the crate's reach and are read from, and patched back into, the fixed BMP v3 layout: `biClrUsed` (the crate zero-pads `get_palette` to 256 entries deliberately and exposes the real count nowhere), and both pixels-per-metre fields plus the row order (its encoder hard-codes the first two to 0 and always stores rows bottom-up).

productionDebt.plan: The `image` crate is production-reachable TODAY from two places: the 🎞️animate plugin's video engine and 🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🗺️surface's tiled-map. Discovered by the oracle-purity gate the moment `image` was registered — the gate did its job. Phase 7 target: both call sites want raster decode/encode that ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio already implements, so routing them through decode_bmp / decode_tiff / decode_jpg retires the dependency and this record with it.
